items.title: Contains Duplicate aur Valid Anagram: ek hash map se dono
items.one_idea: Both Contains Duplicate and Valid Anagram are answered by remembering what you have already seen in a hash-based structure (a set of seen values, a count of each character), so no sorting or pair-checking is needed.
items.spoken_hook: Contains Duplicate problem, sorting के बिना एक loop में solve!

items.example: EXAMPLE list [4,7,1,9,7,3]: duplicate found at step 5 with a set, 8 pair checks by brute force; without a duplicate [4,7,1,9,3] needs 5 steps with a set, 10 pair checks. EXAMPLE 10,000 numbers worst case: 49,995,000 pair checks vs 10,000 set steps. Anagram: listen and silent give the same counts, both sort to [e,i,l,n,s,t]; rat and car differ.
items.pattern: remember what you have seen: seen set / frequency count in a hash map
items.check_question: Is [3,8,3] a duplicate? And are 'aab' and 'abb' anagrams? (answers: yes, no; in the caption)
facts_to_verify: Contains Duplicate: hash table O(n) time and O(n) space, sorting O(n log n) time (doocs page 0217, fetched by the planner 2026-10-27).
Valid Anagram: counting is O(n) time and O(C) space with C=26 for lowercase letters (doocs page 0242, fetched).

Counter is a dict subclass for counting hashable objects (Python docs, fetched); hash table average search/insert Theta(1), worst case O(n) (Wikipedia, fetched): say 'average', and name the worst case once as in d008.

Run the code and show its real output: set check on [4,7,1,9,7,3] returns True at step 5, [4,7,1,9,3] returns False after 5 steps; brute force 8 and 10 comparisons; 10,000 numbers = 49,995,000 pairs; Counter('listen')==Counter('silent') True, Counter('rat')==Counter('car') False, Counter('aab')==Counter('abb') False, sorted('listen')==sorted('silent') True (planner ran all of these 2026-10-27; builder re-runs).
Problems are paraphrased from the doocs mirror (LeetCode itself not fetched); do not claim a company asks them.
Keep to ONE idea in the script: remember what you have seen. Anagram constraint is lowercase letters; for Unicode the counting idea stays the same (page follow-up), say only that.
